We learn, We achieve, We flourish
Welcome to East Huntspill Primary School, part of Pathway Trust
We believe that all pupils, regardless of ability or background, will achieve their full potential in a positive and caring environment where all children and families are respected and valued.
We offer a broad, engaging and challenging curriculum, underpinned by high quality teaching and learning, which enables all pupils to become confident and independent learners. We provide opportunities for pupils to develop skills which promote self-esteem and confidence in their relationships.
At East Huntspill Primary, we value strong partnerships with our parents/carers, other educational settings and the wider community to ensure that we provide our pupils with the best opportunities to lead happy and successful lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: East Huntspill Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
About Us
Vision and Values
"Do the best you can until you know better. Then when you know better, do better. "
We believe that all pupils, regardless of ability or background, will achieve their full potential in a positive and caring environment where all children and families are respected and valued.
We offer a broad, engaging and challenging curriculum, underpinned by high quality teaching and learning, which enables all pupils to become confident and independent learners. We provide opportunities for pupils to develop skills which promote self-esteem and confidence in their relationships.
At The Huntspills, we value strong partnerships with our parents/carers, other educational settings and the wider community to ensure that we provide our pupils with the best opportunities to lead happy and successful lives.
Recognition and rewards for effort
We recognise and reward learners who go ‘over and above’ our standards.
Learning Champions and pupils chosen for our Hot Chocolate Friday treat are recognised during our weekly celebration assembly.
Although there are tiered awards, our staff understand that a quiet word of personal praise can be as effective as a larger, more public, reward.
Behaviour for Learning
East Huntspill Primary is committed to creating an environment where exemplary behaviour is at the heart of productive learning.
Everyone is expected to maintain the highest standards of personal conduct, to accept responsibility for their behaviour and encourage others to do the same.

Families
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club has been established for many years and provides care of our pupils before school.
Our Breakfast Club supervisors, who are teaching assistants or lunchtime supervisors, take care of the children from 8.00am each morning and offer a range of food and drink that provides our pupils with a nutritious start to the day. Pupils then enjoy games prior to being taken to their classrooms for the start of the school day.
Booking in advance is now required. To book and pay for your Breakfast Club sessions, please book via your Weduc App using ParentPay.
Booking closes at 3pm the day before.
The cost is £2.50 per children, per morning, which includes breakfast.
For more information, please contact your school office.
Please arrive promptly at 8.00am.
After School Enrichment Clubs
We have After School Clubs from 3.15pm till 4.15pm, Monday to Friday. Our clubs offer lots of different enriching activities. Clubs are £2.00 per session, unless managed by an outside provider. Booking and Payments are completed via Weduc ParentPay. Please speak to the School Office for more information.
Term 2 clubs are now available to book.

pageCache.text:
Little Learners Preschool
Little Learners Preschool
Little Learners @ East Huntspill Primary Academy
We have one class in pre-school, known as Little Learners with up to 20 children in the class at any one time. Our preschool team ensure that the pre-school provision meets the expectations set out in the Early Years Foundation Stage, as well as provide opportunities for them to integrate and be part of the academy as a whole. We welcome children aged 2 years and above to learn, explore and have fun through play.
We understand and celebrate the unique qualities in every child, and we ensure our setting is an enjoyable and positive experience for all the children in our care. Our vibrant classroom offers access to a wealth of natural resources and learning opportunities, with the outside area being an extension of the classroom.
How do I sign my child up?
We would be delighted to welcome you at one of our upcoming open days. We recommend you contact us early if you are interested in a place.
To register your interest and find out more about open days, prospective families are requested to submit an eyLog enquiry here.
What are your session times?
8.00am - 8.45am – Breakfast Club
8.45am - 11.45am – Morning
11.45am - 12.15pm – Lunch
12.15pm - 3.15pm – Afternoon
What funding can I access?
If you are looking to apply for funding for 2-year-olds for working families (which came into effect from 1 April 2024), please visit the Childcare Choices page. Use the ‘Apply now’ button under the heading ’15 and 30 hours support’.
Families can get funding for 2-year-olds if they meet the criteria which can be found on the Somerset County Council website.
Children aged three and above will be entitled to either 15 or 30 hours fully funded childcare per week (term time only). If you are looking for more information about what you might be eligible for and when this starts for your child, you can find more information on the Somerset County Council website.
How can I contact you if I have a question?
Please contact us at eastlittlelearners@thpa.theplt.org.uk or call us on 01278 782453, we will be happy to help you.

Families
New starters
Are you and your child interested in joining us at East Huntspill Primary School? Please phone the school on 01278 782453 or email east@thpa.theplt.org.uk to book an appointment to have a look around our lovely school. We also occasionally have spaces in other year groups, please contact the school to enquire about availability. We would love to hear from you.

Apply to start school for the first time
Choosing the right school is one of the most important decisions you will make for your child's future. To help you experience what makes East Huntspill Primary School so unique, we warmly invite you to visit us and take a look around.
A school tour is the perfect opportunity to see our vibrant community in action. During your visit, you will be able to:
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to East Huntspill Primary School.
Please click on the link below for any In Year school admissions:
In year School Admissions
Gates open from 8:30am. Between 8.30 -8.45am, children take part in learning activities to encourage a calm, confident start to the school day. The registers are taken at 8:45am, if a child arrives after that, they will be marked as Late. Children have a mid-morning break for 15 minutes. Our under 5's are able to have a glass of milk and all children are invited to have a piece of fruit for a snack. Our lunchtime is 12:00-1:00pm and the day finishes at 3:15pm. Please wait in the playground and children will be escorted out by their class teacher.
We have Breakfast and After-School clubs available daily. Pre-booking is essential. Please book through the Reach More Parents App.
Children at East Huntspill Primary are expected to wear the school uniform which is blue, grey and white. We believe that by wearing a uniform, children develop a sense of pride in and identify with their school. We encourage all children to look smart during their time at school. All uniforms with a school logo on them can be purchased from https://price-buckland.co.uk/. We also encourage parents to buy generic uniform items from local supermarkets and high street stores to help keep costs affordable. We also hold a selection of pre-loved uniforms available from the school office.
All children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 are able to receive free Universal School Meals. These meals are provided by Aspens catering at The King Alfred School Academy in Highbridge. The menu is provided on a 3-weekly basis and parents are asked to discuss and complete a menu with their child on the Aspens Select website. As your child progresses into older years, you are able to purchase these meals through the same website.
Children will need to bring their own labelled drinking bottles every day, filled with water only.
All communication is through an App called Weduc – Reach More Parents. You will be given more information regarding the app upon your child joining us. Occasionally we do need to print letters out to go home. These will be sent home in your child’s book bag.

Our Learning
Behaviour for Learning
"To give our children roots and wings"
At East Huntspill Primary, we passionately believe that everyone should feel happy, valued, and included; individuality is recognised and celebrated. We strive to provide pupils with a safe, nurturing and loving environment that provides them with a deep understanding that they can achieve extraordinary and incredible things!
We trust our children to make the right decisions that are right for them and to challenge themselves in their own learning, asking questions and deepening their understanding of the world around them.
Independence is promoted and children are encouraged to be actively involved in their learning.
We work together to ensure co-agency whereby we work collaboratively to solve problems and to develop our curriculum. We also promote collaboration between parents and the wider community as we are very aware of the vital role that they play in school life.
Unpredictability is actively encouraged! We believe that children should be encouraged to surprise us with their ideas and what they can do. Our history does not define our destiny, and we are therefore committed to the concept of being unpredictable!

pageCache.pageTitle: East Huntspill Primary School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Learning
Our Curriculum
'Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world'
Intent
Our curriculum has been well-designed with the aim of helping children develop a deep love of learning. It is far more than simply the subjects we teach; our intention is that our children leave our schools with strong characters and the passion and knowledge to make a positive contribution to our world. We believe that learners are at their most successful when their imagination is stimulated, their curiosity is heightened and their learning makes links to their own lives and the wider world.
Our curriculum is a balance of discrete subject teaching where appropriate and is taught through big questions which foster enquiry-led learning experiences. It is infused with experiential learning and authentic contexts that engage children in their local area before moving further afield, ensuring that all learners have a clear sense of self and a sense of place. Children are at the heart of the curriculum. We ensure that our well-sequenced, progressive, ambitious curriculum starts with our youngest learners through what questions, develops to how in lower key stage 2 and progresses to answering why questions by the end of their primary years.
Cognitive development, emotional literacy and vocabulary development underpin our approach. Our big questions are created from the National Curriculum to ensure that children develop their curiosity and are able to formulate and present an answer through a ‘presentation of understanding’ which requires the children to share their learning with others. In this way, they not only learn knowledge but practice character traits such as collaboration, communication and courage.
The core intention of our curriculum is for our children to develop a deep body of substantive and disciplinary knowledge ensuring that every child knows more, can remember more and can do more. Alongside the substantive bank of knowledge and skills, children are encouraged to develop ‘states of being’ where they can think like a subject specialist. This enables our children and teachers to make connections across subjects.
Our curriculum is underpinned by cognitive development, anchoring all aspects of learning to reinforce personal identity and the present day, essential in creating self-aware individuals. As they develop, we will strive to help them connect to the immediate environment/ community/ country until they are able to conceptualise abstract themes. Children are immersed in quality texts which support the development of a rich vocabulary and a real understanding of stories. Through clear, planned progression, the curriculum has woven knowledge, skills, vocabulary and concepts throughout all the enquiries studied. The curriculum has strong links with the local area and the UK and has links to significant people, places and events within the locality and beyond.
The curriculum prepares children to live in their world and to be able to contribute as knowledgeable, responsible and compassionate citizens. Humanitarian values are integral throughout the curriculum and contribute to the legacy that we give to the world through the generations of children that journey through our school.
Implementation
At East Huntspill, we teach the National Curriculum through 21 x 12 week learning enquiries in Reception to year six; three per year for each year group. English and mathematics are taught discretely although are also linked to the wider curriculum, learning where appropriate. Each learning enquiry incorporates mini enquiry questions/ milestones.
Each learning enquiry builds upon prior learning and concepts are mapped across to ensure that children have the opportunity to build upon existing knowledge, revisiting and understanding more as they go. Our history curriculum is organised chronologically in terms of British history from KS2 onwards. World history builds upon concepts learnt from one learning enquiry to the next. Examples of key concepts studied include exploration, settlement, power, chronology etc.
Impact
The impact of our curriculum will be measured by ascertaining how much children know and can do from one learning enquiry to the next. We will evaluate what knowledge and understanding our children have gained against age-related expectations.
"Learning is defined as an alteration in long term memory. If nothing has been altered in long-term memory-nothing has been learnt"
Assessment will be part of everyday classroom practice, combining a responsive teaching approach with time given to children to make improvements and correct misconceptions. As well as ongoing assessment, at the end of each learning enquiry, a dedicated cycle of Review, Revise and Reflect will include opportunities for summative assessments (including nationalised tests, self and peer quizzes) and the revision of skills and knowledge and an opportunity to reflect on learning. This could be through celebration of learning events, including presentations, published pieces, art galleries and class museums etc.
If you would like any further information on our curriculum, please contact the Headteacher, Emma Barker.

About Us
SEND
Inclusion: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Information
East Huntspill Primary School is a school where everyone is valued, trusted and all individuals are included and welcome – we are a true ‘Learning without Limits’ school. We believe that all children can become more powerful, committed and successful learners when provided with supportive and inclusive conditions and generous opportunities for individualised learning. We know that children thrive best in a nurturing environment where all of their achievements are valued and celebrated.
Our SENDCo, Rachel Hine, with support from Headteacher, Emma Barker, is available via email east@thpa.theplt.org.uk or the school office for parents consultations.
If you have any concerns about your child’s progress at school regarding any area of their learning, the first person to speak to about your concerns is your child’s class teacher. If you still have any ongoing concerns, you may wish to speak to the school’s SENDCo.
If any educational needs are identified, Rachel Hine and the class teacher, with the support of Emma Barker, will plan how to provide support for your child with the involvement of both yourself and the class teacher and outside agencies as appropriate. We follow an assess, plan, do, review cycle.
If additional support is needed, we will work closely with families and outside agencies to overcome any barriers children may face in their learning.
Families are offered the opportunity to meet their child’s class teacher twice a year at Learning Review Meetings to discuss their progress.
Mrs Moffatt, our Learning Mentor is available to meet with families to discuss any social and emotional issues which they feel may be affecting their child’s ability to learn. They can work with small groups and/or with individual children depending on the child’s specific needs. Appointments can be arranged via the school office.
If you still have concerns that your child’s needs are not being met, please do speak to Emma Barker.
Useful Information
Somerset’s Graduated Response Tool
Somerset’s Graduated Response Tool now replaces the Somerset Core Standards. This has been co-produced with stakeholders from education, health, social care, parent carers and support service teams. Somerset’s Graduated Response Tool sets out the barriers to learning that children and young people may have and the strategies and provision that could be in place to support them. To find out more information, follow the link: Somerset's Graduated Response Tool

About Us
Parent and Family Support ( PFSA)
"The most important thing in the world is family and love."
-John Wooden
What is a PFSA?
Parent and Family Support Advisors (PFSAs) work with school-aged children and their families that require additional support. PFSAs work within Somerset Council’s Early Help Framework to enable high-quality support for children/young people and families at the earliest possible stage.
PFSAs work closely and collaboratively with schools, families and other support services in order to improve attendance, engagement and outcomes for children. The needs of the child/young person or family form the basis of all the work completed. Where there is a need for support from other services, PFSAs can act as the Lead Professional.
PFSAs are only able to engage in work with families with their informed consent and agreement.
Support is based on the needs the child/young person or family has at the time. Support plans are reviewed regularly to ensure needs continue to be met and that progress is made.
What does PFSA support look like?
PFSA support provides weekly or fortnightly visits to help support families to address concerns, worries or challenges. Our PFSA will provide strategies, guidance and resources to support your family's needs.
PFSA support advocates families working together to create a safe, loving and caring home environment.
What can a PFSA help me with?
Our PFSA can offer support in the following areas (but not limited to):
Additionally, we provide workshops for all families with children/young people across the Trust. Families who aren’t receiving PFSA support through the rolling programme may also attend. Examples of workshops include behaviour management, sleep hygiene, healthy eating, behaviour management.
We also host coffee mornings and workshops with external agencies such as Weston Hospice, the school nursing team, MHST etc.
School refusal, attendance and emotional-based school avoidance
Behaviour management (anger, big emotions, anxiety)
Boundaries and routines
Anxiety/separation anxiety
Grief and bereavement
Emotional coaching and processing
Child on parent abuse
Sleep routines
Personal hygiene
How can I receive PFSA support?
Speak to your school’s Designated Safeguarding Lead, Learning Mentor or Headteacher. The school will place an Early Help Assessment referral and submit it to our PFSA. Our PFSA will be in contact as soon as possible.
How can I get in touch?
For more information or to reach out directly, please contact your school or email Kelly at PFSA@theplt.org.uk

About Us
About Us
Welcome to East Huntspill Primary School – We are part of The Priory Learning Trust.
We are a friendly, nurturing small village school with big ambitions. We sit at the heart of our local community and inspire our children through lighting up a love of learning. We are a caring, inclusive family school where everyone is welcome.
We have the highest expectations of our learners through all aspects of school life and beyond. Understanding, acceptance and respect for others is fostered throughout our school and this is reflected through excellent learning and behaviour. We are blessed to have a large playing field, and beautiful grounds which enhance our love of outdoor learning.
There is a great deal of information available to you on this website and via our social media platforms, but the best way to get to know our school is to come and see us. Every day is an open day at East Huntspill Primary, so if you would like to come and visit, please get in touch. We look forward to meeting you.
